text: The length of the latus-rectum of the ellipse, whose foci are $(2,5)$ and $(2,-3)$ and eccentricity is $\frac{4}{5}$, is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To find the length of the latus rectum of the ellipse, we first recognize that the foci of the ellipse are given as $F_{1}:(2,5)$ and $F_{2}:(2,-3)$. This indicates that the major axis is aligned along the $y$-axis.

Calculate the distance between the foci:

$F_{1}F_{2}=8$

The formula involving the distance between the foci and the eccentricity is:

$F_{1}F_{2}=2be$

Here, the eccentricity $e$ is given as $\frac{4}{5}$. Thus, we can solve for $b$:

$8=2b\cdot \frac{4}{5}⟹b=\frac{8}{2\times \frac{4}{5}}=5$

Determine $a^{2}$:

Using the relationship between eccentricity, semi-minor axis $b$, and semi-major axis $a$:

$e^{2}=1-\frac{a^{2}}{b^{2}}=1-\frac{a^{2}}{25}=\frac{16}{25}$

Solving for $a^{2}$:

$1-\frac{a^{2}}{25}=\frac{16}{25}⟹\frac{a^{2}}{25}=\frac{9}{25}⟹a^{2}=9$

Thus, $a=3$.

Compute the length of the latus rectum:

The formula for the length of the latus rectum $L$ is:

$L=\frac{2a^{2}}{b}$

Substituting the known values:

$L=\frac{2\times (9)}{5}=\frac{18}{5}$

Therefore, the length of the latus rectum of the ellipse is $\frac{18}{5}$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift

text: $1+3+5^{2}+7+9^{2}+\ldots$ upto 40 terms is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Step 1: Breaking the sequence into two parts

The given sequence is $1+3+5^{2}+7+9^{2}+\ldots$ up to 40 terms. Let's group the terms as follows:

The terms are arranged like this: $1$, $3$, $5^{2}$, $7$, $9^{2}$, $11$, $13^{2}$, $15$, $17^{2}$, ... You can see that every alternate term is being squared, while others are just numbers. So, split the sequence into: all squared terms ($1^{2},5^{2},9^{2},...$) and all other numbers ($3,7,11,...$).

Step 2: Counting the terms in each group

Out of 40 terms, half will be squared terms and half will be non-squared terms. So we have 20 squared terms and 20 ordinary numbers.

Step 3: Sums for each group

The squared numbers follow this pattern: $1^{2},5^{2},9^{2},...$, which can be written as $(4k-3)^{2}$ for $k$ from 1 to 20.

The other numbers are $3,7,11,...,(4k-1)$ for $k$ from 1 to 20.

Step 4: Write these as formulas

Total sum = Sum of squares part $+$ Sum of ordinary numbers part.

The sum of the squared numbers is $\sum\limits _{k=1}^{20}(4k-3)^{2}$.

The sum of the other numbers (arithmetic series): $3+7+11+...$ for 20 terms. 

The first term is 3, the last term is $3+(20-1)\times 4=3+76=79$. So, the sum is $\frac{20}{2}[3+79]=10\times 82=820$.

Step 5: Expanding and simplifying

Expand $(4k-3)^{2}$:

$(4k-3)^{2}=16k^{2}-24k+9$

So, sum up these for $k=1$ to $20$:

$16\sum k^{2}-24\sum k+9\times 20$

We know formulas:

$\sum\limits _{k=1}^{n}k^{2}=\frac{n(n+1)(2n+1)}{6}$

$\sum\limits _{k=1}^{n}k=\frac{n(n+1)}{2}$

Plug in $n=20$:

$\sum\limits _{k=1}^{20}k^{2}=\frac{20\times 21\times 41}{6}$

$\sum\limits _{k=1}^{20}k=\frac{20\times 21}{2}$

Now, sum up:

$=16\left (\frac{20\times 21\times 41}{6}\right )-24\left (\frac{20\times 21}{2}\right )+180+820$

Step 6: Calculating

$16\left (\frac{20\times 21\times 41}{6}\right )=16\times 2870=45920$

$24\left (\frac{20\times 21}{2}\right )=24\times 210=5040$

$9\times 20=180$

Sum of the other numbers = $820$

So, total = $45920-5040+180+820$

$=45920-5040=40880$

$40880+180=41060$

$41060+820=41880$

Final Answer

The sum of the 40 terms is $41880$.

$\begin{array}{ll} \Rightarrow  & 25x^{2}-20x+4=0 \\ \quad (5x-2)^{2}=0\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{2}{5} \\ \Rightarrow  & \cos ^{2}θ=\dfrac{2}{5}\Rightarrow \sin ^{2}θ=\dfrac{3}{5}, \\ \quad \sec ^{2}θ=\dfrac{5}{2},\mathrm{cosec}^{2}θ=\dfrac{5}{3} \end{array}$

$I=\int\limits _{0}^{1}\left (1+\sqrt{2}x^{1/2}\right )dx=1+\sqrt{2}\cdot \dfrac{2}{3}=1+\dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{3}$

Hence, the correct option is (A).

$15^{\text{th}}$ term from beginning: $T_{15}={}^{n}C_{14}a^{n-14}b^{14}$
$15^{\text{th}}$ term from end: $T_{15}^{'}={}^{n}C_{14}b^{n-14}a^{14}$

$\begin{array}{l} \therefore \quad \dfrac{T_{15}}{T_{15}^{'}}=\dfrac{1}{6} \\ \left (\dfrac{a}{b}\right )^{n-28}=\dfrac{1}{6} \\ \left (6^{\frac{1}{3}}\right )^{n-28}=6^{-1} \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{n-28}{3}=-1 \\ n=25 \\ \therefore \quad {}^{25}C_{3}=2300 \end{array}$

text: Considering the principal values of the inverse trigonometric functions, $\sin ^{-1}\left (\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}x+\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\right ),-\frac{1}{2}<x<\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$, is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $𝜙=\sin ^{-1}x$, so $x=\sin 𝜙$. Since $-\dfrac{1}{2}<x<\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$, $-\dfrac{π}{6}<𝜙<\dfrac{π}{4}$, so $\cos 𝜙>0$ and $\sqrt{1-x^{2}}=\cos 𝜙$.

$\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}x+\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{1-x^{2}}=\sin 𝜙\cos \frac{π}{6}+\cos 𝜙\sin \frac{π}{6}=\sin \left (𝜙+\frac{π}{6}\right )$

Here $0<𝜙+\dfrac{π}{6}<\dfrac{5π}{12}$, which lies in $\left [-\dfrac{π}{2},\dfrac{π}{2}\right ]$, so

$\sin ^{-1}\left (\sin \left (𝜙+\frac{π}{6}\right )\right )=𝜙+\frac{π}{6}=\frac{π}{6}+\sin ^{-1}x$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift

text: Let $C$ be the circle $x^{2}+(y-1)^{2}=2,E_{1}$ and $E_{2}$ be two ellipses whose centres lie at the origin and major axes lie on x -axis and y -axis respectively. Let the straight line $x+y=3$ touch the curves $C,E_{1}$ and $E_{2}$ at $P(x_{1},y_{1}),Q(x_{2},y_{2})$ and $R(x_{3},y_{3})$ respectively. Given that $P$ is the mid point of the line segment $QR$ and $PQ=\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{3}$, the value of $9(x_{1}y_{1}+x_{2}y_{2}+x_{3}y_{3})$ is equal to $_______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The circle $x^{2}+(y-1)^{2}=2$ has centre $(0,1)$ and radius $\sqrt{2}$. Its distance from $x+y=3$ is $\dfrac{|0+1-3|}{\sqrt{2}}=\sqrt{2}$, so the line touches it at the foot of the perpendicular from the centre:

$P=(0,1)+(1,1)=(1,2)\Rightarrow x_{1}y_{1}=2$

An ellipse $\dfrac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$ has tangent $\dfrac{xx_{0}}{a^{2}}+\dfrac{yy_{0}}{b^{2}}=1$ at $(x_{0},y_{0})$. Matching it with $\dfrac{x}{3}+\dfrac{y}{3}=1$ gives the point of contact $\left (\dfrac{a^{2}}{3},\dfrac{b^{2}}{3}\right )$, and this point lies on the ellipse only if $a^{2}+b^{2}=9$.

$Q$ and $R$ lie on $x+y=3$ with $P$ as mid point and $PQ=PR=\dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{3}$, so they are $(1\pm \frac{2}{3},2\mp \frac{2}{3})$, that is $\left (\dfrac{5}{3},\dfrac{4}{3}\right )$ and $\left (\dfrac{1}{3},\dfrac{8}{3}\right )$.

For $E_{1}$ (major axis on the x-axis) $a^{2}>b^{2}$, so its contact point has $x_{2}>y_{2}$: $Q=\left (\dfrac{5}{3},\dfrac{4}{3}\right )$ with $a^{2}=5,b^{2}=4$. For $E_{2}$ (major axis on the y-axis) $R=\left (\dfrac{1}{3},\dfrac{8}{3}\right )$ with $a^{2}=1,b^{2}=8$; both satisfy $a^{2}+b^{2}=9$.


[IMG]

$9(x_{1}y_{1}+x_{2}y_{2}+x_{3}y_{3})=9\left (2+\dfrac{20}{9}+\dfrac{8}{9}\right )=18+20+8=46$

Hence, the answer is 46.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift

text: Let $m$ and $n$ be the number of points at which the function $f(x)=\max \left \{x,x^{3},x^{5},\ldots x^{21}\right \},x\in \mathrm{ℝ}$, is not differentiable and not continuous, respectively. Then $m+n$ is equal to $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For $x\geq 1$: $x^{21}\geq x^{19}\geq \cdots \geq x$, so $f(x)=x^{21}$.

For $0\leq x<1$: higher powers are smaller, $x\geq x^{3}\geq \cdots \geq x^{21}$, so $f(x)=x$.

For $-1\leq x<0$: every odd power is negative and $|x^{21}|\leq |x^{19}|\leq \cdots \leq |x|$, so $x^{21}$ is the largest and $f(x)=x^{21}$.

For $x<-1$: every odd power is negative and $|x|<|x^{3}|<\cdots <|x^{21}|$, so $x$ is the largest and $f(x)=x$.

$f(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} x, & x<-1 \\ x^{21}, & -1\leq x\leq 0 \\ x, & 0<x<1 \\ x^{21}, & x\geq 1 \end{array} \right.$

The pieces agree at $x=-1$ (value $-1$), at $x=0$ (value $0$) and at $x=1$ (value $1$), so $f$ is continuous everywhere and $n=0$.

The derivative is $1$ where $f(x)=x$ and $21x^{20}$ where $f(x)=x^{21}$. At $x=-1$: $f^{'}(-1^{-})=1$, $f^{'}(-1^{+})=21$. At $x=0$: $f^{'}(0^{-})=0$, $f^{'}(0^{+})=1$. At $x=1$: $f^{'}(1^{-})=1$, $f^{'}(1^{+})=21$.

The one-sided derivatives differ at all three points, so $f$ is not differentiable at $x=-1,0,1$ and $m=3$.

$m+n=3+0=3$.

Hence, the answer is 3.

text: Let $A=\left [\begin{array}{lll} \cos θ & 0 & -\sin θ \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ \sin θ & 0 & \cos θ \end{array}\right ]$. If for some $θ\in (0,π),A^{2}=A^{T}$, then the sum of the diagonal elements of the matrix $(\mathrm{A}+\mathrm{I})^{3}+(\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{I})^{3}-6\mathrm{A}$ is equal to $_________$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Note that $A$ is orthogonal:

$AA^{T}=A^{T}A=I\text{and}A^{T}=A^{-1}$

Given $A^{2}=A^{T}$, then:

$\begin{array}{l} A^{3}=I \\ \mathrm{Tr}(A+I)^{3}+(A-I)^{3}-6A=\mathrm{Tr}\left (2A^{3}+6A-6A\right ) \\ =\mathrm{Tr}\left (2A^{3}\right )=\mathrm{Tr}(2I) \\ \left (\text{Using}(A+I)^{3}+(A-I)^{3}=2A^{3}+6A\text{and}2A^{3}=2I\right )= \\ 6 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift

text: If the area of the region $\{(x,y):|x-5|\leq y\leq 4\sqrt{x}\}$ is $A$, then $3A$ is equal to $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


$\begin{array}{l} \text{Area}=\int\limits _{1}^{25}4\sqrt{x}dx-\dfrac{1}{2}\times (5-1)\cdot 4-\dfrac{1}{2}\times (25-5)\times 20 \\ =4\left [\dfrac{2}{3}x^{\frac{3}{2}}\right ]_{1}^{25}-8-200=\dfrac{368}{3} \\ \Rightarrow 3A=368 \end{array}$
